# Vantor T60

A 2019 Vantor T60 D4 Momentum, bought used in 2023 with 41,000 miles on it. This
note is long on purpose: it holds six substantial sections, so it chunks into
several pieces and is the note that demonstrates single-source dominance in a
result set of five.

## Identifiers

Vehicle reference VEH-88412 with the insurer, first registered 14 March 2019. The
VIN is stamped on the plate at the base of the windscreen on the passenger side as
well as being printed inside the service book, and is not written down here. The
engine number is T4204X14-889201. The V5C is filed with the purchase paperwork and
names two previous keepers, both of them lease companies, which is consistent
with the service history being complete and main-dealer until 2023. The key
fobs are numbered on the inside of the plastic shell, 1 and 2, and the spare
wheel is a space saver rather than a full-size, rated to 50mph.

## Service history

Serviced annually regardless of mileage, because the oil in this engine degrades
on time rather than distance and the service interval the car itself reports is
optimistic. The full history reads: 2019 to 2022 main dealer, stamped, four
services; 2023 an independent Vantor specialist in Peterborough, oil and filter
plus brake fluid; 2024 the same specialist, oil, filter, air filter and pollen
filter; 2025 oil, filter, fuel filter and a gearbox oil change at 71,000 miles;
2026 oil, filter and the second brake fluid change. Every invoice is scanned and
filed. ### Paperwork

Every invoice from 2023 onward is scanned and held with the service book. The two
main-dealer stamps from 2019 and 2020 exist only as stamps, with no invoice, which
is normal for a lease car and is worth knowing before anyone goes looking for them.

The cambelt is a 10-year or 150,000-mile item on this engine and is
therefore due in 2029 on time rather than on mileage, which is the single
largest piece of scheduled spend outstanding on the car.

## Tyres and wheels

Fitted with 235/45 R18 on the standard five-spoke alloys. The current set is
Arden AllSeason 2, fitted all round in 2025 at 6.8mm, and measured at
4.9mm on the fronts and 5.8mm on the rears in September 2026. The fronts wear
roughly twice as fast as the rears on this car, which is normal for a
front-biased all-wheel-drive layout. Pressures are 2.4 bar front and 2.2 bar
rear for normal loading, and the placard inside the driver's door gives the
laden figures. One alloy, the nearside rear, is kerbed and has been refurbished
once already.

## Faults and fixes

Three faults worth recording. First, the AdBlue level sensor read erratically
through 2024 and threw a no-start warning at 400 miles of range remaining; the
sensor was replaced under a goodwill contribution from Vantor. Second, the
tailgate strut on the offside weakened and the tailgate began dropping in cold
weather, replaced as a pair in 2025 because replacing one strut on its own
unbalances the tailgate. Third, an intermittent whine from the fuel pump at low
tank levels, present since purchase, investigated twice and never reproduced on
a diagnostic, and which has caused no symptom other than the noise.

## Consumption and costs

Real-world consumption sits at 48.2 mpg over a rolling year, against a claimed
combined figure well above that. Motorway cruising at 70 returns 56 mpg and
short winter journeys return 34 mpg, which is the spread that makes the annual
average the only useful number. Annual running cost, excluding depreciation and
insurance, has averaged 1,310 across servicing, tyres, the two faults that were
not covered and 8,000 miles of fuel. Road tax is 195 a year on the standard
rate, and the car falls outside the expensive-car supplement because its list
price when new was under the threshold.

## Paperwork

The V5C, the purchase invoice, the two remaining service invoices not yet
scanned, the tyre fitting receipt and the MOT certificates from 2022 onward are
all held physically in the folder in the study. The MOT is due each March and
has never produced an advisory other than tyre wear. The warranty from the
independent specialist covers parts they supplied for 12 months and is the
reason to keep using them rather than the cheaper garage in town.
